findings.finding: Synchronous authorization and adapter-description work can exhaust the deadline after health but before execute; dispatch does not recheck it.
findings.reproduction: A 20 ms task deadline and 40 ms valid authority lookup activated by health still dispatch once, then return deadline-exhausted.
findings.requiredClosure: Check the effective deadline immediately before execute and cover deadline passage during authorization.

findings.boundary: model registry permission, routing reservations and persisted attempt authority
findings.finding: Current permission cost is checked per attempt while cumulative reservations use only RoutingPolicy. A caller restriction cannot enlarge permission authority.
findings.reproduction: Permission cap 5, RoutingPolicy cap 100 and cost 5 per attempt allow two dispatches after one rate-limited failure, reserving 10.
findings.requiredClosure: Intersect cumulative reservations with current permission and policy caps before dispatch and output; retain reservations across retry/fallback and bind the effective cap in attempt evidence.

findings.finding: Python type-parameter names are absent from lexical shadowing detection, allowing an unrelated generic annotation to inherit the async Protocol exemption.
findings.reproduction: Import Compute as Port, then define async def run[Port](adapter: Port) and await adapter.execute(task); the checker wrongly exempts the call.
findings.requiredClosure: Revoke ambiguous exemptions for TypeVar, ParamSpec and TypeVarTuple bindings and retain pinned-runtime regression fixtures.
